messages.author: fa6f5d4c13c0cca5
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error with scale/correlation decomposition of covariance matrix in mixed effect model
parts:
Is there any reason the default inits aren't working for you? Stan is usually pretty good with that.

You also may wish to use the cholesky parameterization for correlation matrices; in many cases they tend to be more stable and efficient. It would also let you use the non-central multivariate normal. Finally, poisson_log(lambda) is more numerically stable than poisson(exp(lambda)). There is a pretty good description of most of this in the manual, if you are unfamiliar with it.

Actually I don't know: I tried different things, default parametrs aren't working, but when I use stan_model it compiles fine. 

I found a little code for the inital parameters: 

Posdef <- function (n, ev = runif(n, 0, 10)) 
{
  Z <- matrix(ncol=n, rnorm(n^2))
  decomp <- qr(Z)
  Q <- qr.Q(decomp) 
  R <- qr.R(decomp)
  d <- diag(R)
  ph <- d / abs(d)
  O <- Q %*% diag(ph)
  Z <- t(O) %*% diag(ev) %*% O
  return(Z)
}

which creates positive definite matrices, but I still get an error. I'll go through the documentation to find something, thank you

Sampling works fine, I don't get many warning concerning covariance/correlation matrices. I want to share what worked for me (now I'm working just with fixed effects beta and product specific mixed effects eta).

What I did:

  • introduce a fixed intercept term
  • using poisson_log(lambda) instead of poisson(exp(lambda))
  • specify the correlation and covariance matrices as unconstrained matrices
  •  initializing the covariance and correlation matrices as symmetric positive definite matrices
I wonder there's a reason why these step worked for now (I'll now introduce group effects), but I can assure that I did some sort of step search so there is not collinearity in the steps above. 
Once finished I'll put the stan code so that newcomers as me could have a lil more help. 

Thank you again

Just catching up with some back messages.

If you don't have strong priors, the covariance and correlation
matrices and overflow/underflow in the corners so you wind up
with bad matrices due to arithmetic or step sizes being too large.

More regularization and/or higher adapt_delta should help.

- Bob
